upcoming.title: Pilates in the Garden (Tuesdays)
upcoming.body:
Step away from the everyday and reconnect with your body in the beautiful surroundings of the Miami Beach Botanical Garden.

Join The Pilates Place Studios for a rejuvenating Classical Mat Pilates class led by Victoria Collins, rooted in the original method developed by Joseph Pilates. This full-body practice combines mindful movement, focused breathing, core strength, mobility, and control to leave you feeling stronger, longer, and more connected to your body.

Whether you are new to Pilates or have been practicing for years, this class offers an opportunity to experience the timeless Pilates method in a relaxed, inspiring outdoor setting.

Expect a thoughtfully guided mat class that honors the classical sequence while making the practice accessible and enjoyable for all levels. Come move, breathe, strengthen, and reset surrounded by nature.

What to bring: A Pilates or yoga mat, water, and comfortable clothing.

No previous Pilates experience necessary.

Come for the movement. Stay for the feeling. 🌿

About Victoria Collins:

Victoria is a Miami-based Pilates instructor with a background in education and a passion for mind-body alignment through intentional movement and breathwork. Victoria discovered mat Pilates at age 16 during a time when she was navigating her own mental health and physical wellness challenges. She immediately fell in love with the method as a powerful tool to regain control of her body and calm her mind. Years later, her sister-in-law introduced her to Pilates classes using the reformer at The Pilates Place Studios. This introduction reignited that initial spark, inspiring her to complete her Pilates teacher training at The Pilates Place Studios so she could help others experience the transformative power of the practice.

Victoria firmly believes that Pilates is for every body—regardless of age, background, or fitness level. Her classes combine classical and contemporary techniques into a challenging, full-body workout powered by the breath. Expect a warm, supportive, and encouraging environment where you can build mobility, strength, balance, and mind-body awareness.

upcoming.title: In the Lab: The Little Wetland
upcoming.body:
The ecological intimacy of a swamp, none of the physical inconveniences. In the Lab: The Little Wetland brings children face-to-face with living swamp flora, including aquatic carnivorous plants. Children study the plants in individual aquariums, then come together to create a miniature living wetland in a shallow vessel.


About Sasha Sikaffy:

Sasha S. Sikaffy, M.S., is an environmental scientist and educator informed by years spent in coral reef fieldwork and marine science education.

Her work considers how children come to know the living world through direct ecological encounter—attention to living systems, intimacy with place, and sustained contact with the more-than-human world.

In The Lab is her ongoing study of South Florida ecology, in which children engage with living organisms, biological specimens, and scientific instruments across field and lab settings.


Important Information:

Designed for children ages 4-8, with one accompanying adult per child.

All materials and scientific tools are provided.

Comfortable clothing suitable for working with water is recommended, along with a water flask.

upcoming.body:
Join Miami-based musician and artist Bruno Esposito for a hands-on exploration of how plant materials become music. Discover the guacharaca, its Indigenous roots and role in Colombian Caribbean traditions, and the natural materials behind gaitas, maracas, and drums. upcoming.title: The Art of Belonging: A Friendsgiving HypnoExpression
upcoming.body:
HypnoExpression: Meditate • Create • Elevate 
Curated by Joanne Burgess, Founder of Flight of Minds 

A heart-opening afternoon of hypnotherapy meditation, creative expression through art, and somatic dance - each woven together to soothe loneliness, deepen connection, and awaken the power of community. 

Through guided hypnomeditation, guests will gently release emotional walls and open the heart to authentic connection. They will then bring their inner world to life through expressive art - a visual reflection of belonging, gratitude, and shared humanity. The journey continues in a joyful circle of movement and expression, celebrating friendship, compassion, and the beauty of being seen and understood. 

This Friendsgiving-inspired experience invites participants to reconnect with themselves, with others, and with the warmth that comes from genuine human connection. 

No experience is needed - only an open heart and a willingness to receive. 

General Admission: $37 | Members Price: $33

upcoming.title: Nature. In Community
upcoming.body:
On Sunday, November 15, the Miami Beach Botanical Garden transforms into an open landscape of participatory installations—a living laboratory of the senses.

Move freely through interactive stations across the garden: weave, touch, smell, listen, and contribute to an evolving collective creation.

The Experience

  • Participatory Installations: Engage with natural fibers, botanical scents, tactile native elements, and acoustic soundscapes.

  • Collective Making: Contribute your individual gestures of writing, weaving, and reflection into shared works that evolve in real time.

  • Guest Artists: Featuring creative collaborations with guest artists Anna Biondo and Sarah Laing.

The Vision

Created by neuroscientist and artist Karina Del Punta, Ph.D., Nature In Community draws from insights in environmental neuroscience and relational ecology. The work explores what it means to meet the natural world in active reciprocity—rediscovering ourselves not just as visitors or consumers, but as vital participants woven into the fabric of the living landscape.

Through the intentional orchestration of materials, colors, sounds, and scents, the experience invites a state of soft fascination—a restorative mode of attention that calms the nervous system while heightening relational and creative presence. Each individual reflection shared throughout the afternoon weaves into a tangible representation of community and ecological interdependence.

Discover what takes shape when we create together.

upcoming.title: Creative Movement: The Experience
upcoming.body:
Creative Movement: The Experience is a guided moving meditation set within the living energy of the botanical garden. This immersive journey weaves together breathwork, somatic movement, yoga, and meditation—inviting you to slow down, soften, and reconnect to your body in harmony with nature.

We begin with intentional breathwork to ground the nervous system and open awareness, followed by fluid somatic movement and accessible yoga designed to release tension, awaken sensation, and encourage intuitive expression. The experience gently transitions into meditation and stillness, allowing you to fully absorb the rhythms of the garden—its sounds, textures, and natural flow.

This is not about performance or perfection, but presence. You’ll be guided to move as meditation—listening inward, honoring your body, and letting nature lead the pace.

Instructor Bio:

Ashli Katz is a dynamic and visionary fitness professional revolutionizing the industry with a transformative approach to movement and self-discovery. Boasting over a decade of experience in the fitness industry, Ashli has seamlessly blended her foundation in dance, rhythm, movement, and breath into a mesmerizing symphony that takes clients on a captivating journey towards self-reflection, physical prowess, and holistic well-being.

Important info:

  • Materials Required: Yoga mat, towel or light covering for meditation, water.

  • What to wear: Comfortable clothing for moving and resting.

General Admission Price: $55 | Admission for Two: $100 | Members Price: $50

upcoming.title: Rooted in Gratitude: A Sound Bath and Breathwork Journey
upcoming.body:
A breathwork & sound journey into the alchemical power of embodied gratitude.

This 75-minute journey opens seated, beginning with yogic breathing practices that prepare the body and invite presence. From there, you'll move into an active, alchemizing breathwork experience done lying down, moving what feels stagnant, returning you to your essential Self, and attuning you to the wellspring of ease and joy within. The session closes with an immersive sound journey that supports integration and reestablishes inner harmony.

In this season of gratitude, rather than a practice that asks us to overlook our struggles, we expand our awareness to hold difficulty and recognize what is already supportive, already whole, already here — embodying gratitude as the alchemical emotion it truly is.

Walk away feeling lighter, more spacious, and more connected to an inner refuge.

Rooted in ancient wisdom traditions and informed by modern research.

What to Bring:

Feel free to bring a light covering and anything that helps you feel completely at ease—an extra pillow under your head, an eye cover for a deeper experience, or a mat. The more comfortable, the better.

Before You Arrive:

Doors to the Banyan Ballroom close sharply at 6:40 pm so as not to interrupt the experience. We encourage you to arrive early and take in the beauty of the garden — bring your journal or walk the grounds to ground yourself before we begin.

About Franci Blanco:

Franci is a Miami-based wellness facilitator and coach with roughly ten years of experience teaching yoga, breathwork, sound bath, and meditation. She completed her yoga teacher training in Rishikesh, India, and has returned three times since for month-long periods of continued study. She has also completed three ten-day Vipassana meditation retreats and her first year of professional training in the application of therapeutic sound through The Center of Light Institute of Sound Healing and Shamanic Studies. Franci teaches across venues including The Standard and Miami Beach Botanical Garden, and is currently pursuing her Master of Social Work. Her classes are rooted in breath awareness and nervous system support, inviting a deeper connection to the body's own wisdom.

General Admission Price: $50 | Members Price: $45

past.title: Sogetsu Ikebana Class with Sensei Stephan Eberhagen
past.body:
In the Hands-on Sogetsu Ikebana Class, participants will be guided in developing their creativity, mastering specific Ikebana techniques, and exploring the deeper spiritual meaning of this art.

Beginner Class

  1. Check-in & Setup (5 min)

  2. “Get Focused” – Introduction to Basic Upright Style (Moribana) (25 min)

  3. “Get Creative” – Hands-on arrangement creation (45 min)

  4. “Let’s Talk” – Review and discussion (10 min)

  5. Clean-up (5 min)

Materials Required:

  • Suiban (flat container, 8-10” diameter, 2-3” height)

  • Kenzan (flower pin holder, at least 3” diameter)

  • Hasami (Ikebana scissors)

past.title: Building a Learning Garden
past.body:
Andi Potamkin and Muriel Olivares of Little River Cooperative will walk you through how they built a school garden program, and provide you with the information you need to start your own.

This event is open to anyone who is interested in building a learning garden. The featured case-study is a school farm and garden located at the SEED School of Miami in Opa Locka, but the information can be used to build out a learning garden of any size in any location.

Informative handouts will be provided. All attendees need to bring is their curiosity about building a learning garden and their passion for exposing young people to nature.

This event is free to attend.

RSVP

past.title: Folklore & Foliage
past.body:
As darkness falls, the Miami Beach Botanical Garden will transform into a place for the curious and unconventional—a space where forgotten histories come to light, strange ideas take root, and the boundary between the natural and the otherworldly begins to blur.

Join us for this FREE evening where weird is welcomed—art is reimagined, stories are shared, and magic meets creativity.

  • Wander the Garden at night and explore dark art, oddities, and unexpected treasures from participating artisan vendors.

  • “Old Florida” ghost stories from author Thomas Smith, author of The Ghosts of the Florida Atlantic Coast, presented by renowned indie bookstore, Books & Books.

  • Live music by Bruno Esposito of Lone Wolf One Man Band.

  • A site-specific spooky shadow puppet performance by local artist Christina Pettersson.

  • Projected vintage Halloween and haunted South Florida news stories footage courtesy of Miami Dade College’s Lynn and Louis Wolfson II Florida Moving Image Archives.

  • Astrology and tarot readings by Aída the Energy Witch.

  • Personalized poetry by The Biscayne Poet.

  • MBBG's spooky Boo-tanical Bar, food, and more!

This event is free to attend.

RSVP

past.title: Stillness in Motion
past.body:
Find your way back to the present moment through movement, breath, and mindfulness. Set within the living sanctuary of the Garden.

Move through intentional Vinyasa sequences that build functional strength and fluid mobility, anchored in the breath. This is a practice that meets you where you are. Mat required. Water and sunscreen recommended.



About Carolina Jayaram:

A yoga and meditation practitioner for 25 years and a teacher for six, Carolina Jayaram has found these practices to be a steady source of inner wisdom, balance, and renewal. Trained in the Jivamukti and rooted in Patanjali traditions, she leads a practice that leaves the body and mind feeling aligned and fluid. A philanthropic leader, mother, and proud Miami Beach resident, she brings the same belief to her teaching – that when we cultivate stillness within, we become more present, more compassionate, and more capable of building the kind of community we want to call home.

past.title: Perfumer for a Day
past.body:
Under the guidance of Italian perfumer Patrizio Monteleone from Monteleone Fragrances, you’ll explore the aromatic ingredients that bring fragrances to life—from delicate florals to exotic woods and resins

Patrizio, known for blending scent and flavor in his multi-sensory gelato and fragrance creations, will lead you through an unforgettable journey of olfactory discovery.

What to Expect:

  • Introduction to Perfumery - gaining a foundation in fragrance composition, safety, and perfumery principles. Learn what makes a scent balanced, harmonious, and memorable.

past.body:
Live Arts Miami’s MUNDO Live Music Series joins Miami Jazz Booking’s Jazz in the Jungle for an evening at the Miami Beach Botanical Garden featuring Colombian accordionist and cumbia master Yeison Landero, known as El Heredero de la Cumbia (“The Heir of Cumbia”).

The grandson and musical heir of legendary accordionist Andrés Landero, “The King of Cumbia,” Yeison carries the tradition of Colombian cumbia sabanera into a new generation. From his hometown of San Jacinto, Bolívar, to performances at the Hollywood Bowl, The Ford, and Kennedy Center, he has emerged as one of cumbia’s foremost contemporary ambassadors.

The evening marks both the opening of Jazz in the Jungle’s new season and Live Arts Miami’s 2026–27 season, The Art of Together - an invitation to come together through the arts and shared experience. Live music, social dancing, food, drinks, and local vendor activations will unfold throughout the lush setting of the Garden.

Opening set by Miami’s Sonora Tukukuy + Tormenta Tropical Soundsystem, featuring Moonbeam Mike and Oro 11.

past.title: Simplifying Sourdough Baking
past.body:
Join The Lazy Bakers Club to learn the easiest way to make homemade sourdough loaves. You'll take home your own starter and supplies.

This class is perfect for anyone who wants to bake gut-healthy, naturally fermented bread loaves but are afraid it might be too complicated. It's not!

In this class, you'll learn everything you need to be a successful sourdough baker at home, taste test lots of sourdough loaves, and leave class with your own starter and enough dough to bake your loaf at home. No baking experience necessary! This is a hands-on, highly interactive class.

During class you learn:

  • How to prep dough for your loaf

  • How to take care of your starter

  • How to shape your dough for its second proofing

  • How to bake a classic sourdough loaf

  • How to bake a focaccia

During class you receive to take home:

  • sourdough starter

  • spatula

  • ⁠bowl

  • ⁠flour towel

  • ⁠enough dough for a loaf to be baked at home

  • An invitation to our WhatsApp Community to continue learning and connecting with other lazy bakers

  • Printed and digital resources and recipes

You’ll need at home:

  • a kitchen scale

  • ⁠something to bake in (typically a Dutch oven, alternatively a shallow baking pan or cookie sheet)

  • a proofing or banneton basket (this is optional but helpful)

Instructor biography

Laura Rodriguez-Costacamps is the founder and creator of the lazy baker method of sourdough baking, a process that developed from months of experimenting with the simplest way to bake homemade bread. After 15+ years working in science, technology, health, and adult education, Laura became a stay-at-home mom. But the call to educate and experiment persisted and that's how The Lazy Bakers Club was born. Spreading the word of how simple sourdough really is and creating community around experimentation and learning.

General Admission Price: $125 | Members Price: $110

past.title: Tai Chi in the Garden (Wednesdays)
past.body:
Join teacher Silvia Salinas, AP, for Tai Chi in the Garden. The class takes place weekly from 10:00 am - 11:00 am in the Banyan Ballroom or on the patio/lawn (weather permitting).

Designed for beginners, but also enjoyable for long-time practitioners, this class focuses on the foundation of the movements. The health benefits of Tai Chi include improved flexibility, strength, and balance. Through its fluid movements, Tai Chi stimulates deep breathing and blood circulation without straining the heart and other muscles, making it safe for all physical levels.

past.title: Pilates in the Garden (Tuesdays)
past.body:
Step away from the everyday and reconnect with your body in the beautiful surroundings of the Miami Beach Botanical Garden.

Join The Pilates Place Studios for a rejuvenating Classical Mat Pilates class led by Victoria Collins, rooted in the original method developed by Joseph Pilates. This full-body practice combines mindful movement, focused breathing, core strength, mobility, and control to leave you feeling stronger, longer, and more connected to your body.

Whether you are new to Pilates or have been practicing for years, this class offers an opportunity to experience the timeless Pilates method in a relaxed, inspiring outdoor setting.

Expect a thoughtfully guided mat class that honors the classical sequence while making the practice accessible and enjoyable for all levels. Come move, breathe, strengthen, and reset surrounded by nature.

What to bring: A Pilates or yoga mat, water, and comfortable clothing.

No previous Pilates experience necessary.

Come for the movement. Stay for the feeling. 🌿

About Victoria Collins:

Victoria is a Miami-based Pilates instructor with a background in education and a passion for mind-body alignment through intentional movement and breathwork. Victoria discovered mat Pilates at age 16 during a time when she was navigating her own mental health and physical wellness challenges. She immediately fell in love with the method as a powerful tool to regain control of her body and calm her mind. Years later, her sister-in-law introduced her to Pilates classes using the reformer at The Pilates Place Studios. This introduction reignited that initial spark, inspiring her to complete her Pilates teacher training at The Pilates Place Studios so she could help others experience the transformative power of the practice.

Victoria firmly believes that Pilates is for every body—regardless of age, background, or fitness level. Her classes combine classical and contemporary techniques into a challenging, full-body workout powered by the breath. Expect a warm, supportive, and encouraging environment where you can build mobility, strength, balance, and mind-body awareness.

past.title: Little Monster Tales
past.body:
Family-friendly live theatre show promoting literacy, creative writing, self-esteem, poetry, and imaginative thinking.

Discover a world of fun and laughter with Little Monster Tales! Delightfully funny stories from children's books about monsters, children, and other squiggly creatures are brought to life on stage through literature, comedy, puppets, and music. This show is perfect for sparking a love of reading and will have children running to the library for more books by the same authors. Don't be afraid; join us for a ghoulishly good time and end the program with a hilarious monster dance. Little Monster Tales is the trick to making reading a treat!

About Fantasy Theater Factory:

Fantasy Theatre Factory (FTF) is a Not-for-Profit Theater, established in 1978 and incorporated in 1982. FTF is the managing operator of the Sandrell Rivers Theater, a state-of-the-art black box theater in Miami. FTF also has an extensive, statewide and international touring operation.

past.title: Gentle Vinyasa Yoga with Franci
past.body:
A slow, meditative vinyasa practice guided by yogic breath. This class emphasizes subtle body awareness and nervous system support, with helpful verbal cues and gentle assists offered throughout the practice. Through this inward attention, we reconnect with the body’s innate wisdom and integrate that deeper essence into the rhythm of daily life. Each session closes with a longer savasana to rest deeply and absorb the nurturing energy of the garden, supporting integration. 

“It’s not a performance, it’s an inward journey.”

General Admission Price: $22 | Member Price: $20

Follow the winding paths to the Gnome & Fairy Garden and join us for a spooktacular morning at the Miami Beach Boo-tanical Garden.

Children and adults are welcome to join us in creating seasonal crafts and speak with local artist Christina Pettersson.

past.title: Sound Bath Meditation with Franci
past.body:
This immersive soothing sound session is designed to soothe the nervous system and support deep rest. The vibrations of sound help ease tension in the body and invite the nervous system into a more restorative state, offering moments of insight and a deeper connection to the body’s innate wisdom.
